The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data-migration inserts use string interpolation with unescaped SQL; a host value containing a quote breaks the migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration inserts each host with raw string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from `site_settings.value` (free-form text from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting), a value containing a single quote (or other SQL-special characters) will break the SQL and could potentially allow SQL injection during migration. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

The added specs cover controllers/models/store behavior but there is no spec exercising the migration path or verifying legacy data is correctly transformed/removed. adjudication_records.issue_text: Embedding controller update action is a silent no-op, re-rendering the serializer without reading or persisting params

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads `params` or persists anything (it just reuses `@embedding` from `fetch_embedding`, an `OpenStruct` of `EmbeddableHost.all`). However, the UI in this diff manages hosts via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save`, `destroyRecord`), and the `embedding.hbs` template doesn’t invoke `saveChanges`; so this no-op PUT endpoint is more of an unnecessary/unfinished API surface than a clearly user-visible defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Frontend embedding saveChanges calls update({}) and the template has no form fields or save button, making the Embedding settings screen read-only dead UI except for hosts

adjudication.rationale: The `admin-embedding` controller defines a `saveChanges()` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, but the new `embedding.hbs` template never renders a save button nor invokes `saveChanges` at all. The screen is not “read-only dead UI” for its implemented purpose: it provides full CRUD UI for `embedding.embeddable_hosts` via the `embeddable-host` component and the `addHost/deleteHost` actions. The finding assumes there should be additional embedding settings on this screen, but the diff only adds host management here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No uniqueness constraint on EmbeddableHost.host (no validates_uniqueness_of or unique index), allowing duplicates the admin UI cannot disambiguate

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost` only has a format validation (`validates_format_of :host`) and the migration creates `embeddable_hosts.host` with no unique index. This allows duplicate rows for the same host. That causes real incorrect behavior because `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` / `host_allowed?` do `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so with duplicates the selected record (and thus the category used in `TopicEmbed.import` via `eh.try(:category_id)`) becomes arbitrary/non-deterministic. The admin UI also lists by host and category but duplicates of the same host are not prevented at the data layer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec covering duplicate-host submission; embeddable_host model spec tests only protocol/path trimming and host_allowed?

adjudication.rationale: The new EmbeddableHost model/controller allow creating records via Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update, but there’s no uniqueness validation or DB unique index on `embeddable_hosts.host` (model only has `validates_format_of :host`, migration creates no unique constraint). The added model spec (`spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb`) only covers protocol/path trimming and `host_allowed?`, and does not exercise duplicate-host creation/submission behavior. That’s a specific, diff-grounded missing edge-case/test for newly added persistence behavior, but not a strictly verifiable defect without an explicit requirement that duplicates must be rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs only assert AdminController ancestry; no tests for create/update/destroy, authorization (non-staff rejected), or error rendering for invalid host format

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new controllers with nontrivial behavior (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy plus save_host validation/error paths, and Admin::EmbeddingController#show/#update with staff-only access via before_filter). However, the newly added controller specs (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert inheritance from Admin::AdminController and do not exercise CRUD actions, staff/non-staff authorization enforcement, or invalid-host error rendering paths. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No JS test for the embeddable-host component or admin embedding route despite substantial frontend logic

The only JS tests touched are store embedding hydration tests (`test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6` / pretender fixture), and there are no new JS/component/route tests covering the embeddable-host component behavior or the new admin embedding route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Discourse.Category.findById returns undefined for the server-applied uncategorized default, leaving host.category blank after save with no test or handling

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `save()` allows `categoryId` to remain `null`/blank (no validation; `cantSave` only checks host emptiness). The server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) explicitly defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. However, after `host.save(props)`, the client sets `host.category` using `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, which will be `undefined` when `categoryId` was blank, even though the saved record now has a non-blank default category on the server. This can leave `host.category` blank in the UI after save, and there’s no test covering this edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import now uses EmbeddableHost.record_for_host for the category; when no matching host exists imported topics land in no category, changing historical behavior where embed_category applied globally

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` now derives the category from the per-host record: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Since `try` returns `nil` when no record matches, there’s no explicit fallback to the previous global `SiteSetting.embed_category` (which is removed from `site_settings.yml` and `SiteSetting`), so an edge-case caller of `TopicEmbed.import` could create an embedded topic without an intended category. However, other entry points in this diff (e.g., `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`) now block non-allowed hosts via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, so this is more of a completeness/edge-case concern than a clearly verifiable broken behavior in the shown flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The no-matching-host path in TopicEmbed.import is untested; the only added spec tests the happy path with a matching host

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, new logic looks up `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` to `PostCreator` (diff in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`). The added spec (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) fabricates an `embeddable_host` and asserts the imported topic’s category matches it, covering only the matching-host (“happy”) path. There is no new test covering the behavior when `record_for_host(url)` returns nil (no matching host), which is a meaningful edge-case for this new branching behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category fabricators moved verbatim from spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb into spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — unrelated churn with misleading file naming

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was replaced with an `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the previously-existing `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators were moved verbatim into the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. This is real, diff-grounded churn and the new filename is misleading because it now contains category fabricators, not embeddable_host ones.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embedding update action is a no-op: it re-serializes @embedding without applying params, and frontend saveChanges() calls update({}) that persists nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without applying any `params` (new file `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`), so it is indeed a no-op if called. The frontend also defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});` (new `admin-embedding.js.es6`). However, the new `embedding.hbs` template only provides host CRUD via `embeddable-host` component and an `addHost` button; there is no UI invoking `saveChanges`, and host persistence happens via `EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy`. So this looks like unused/incomplete plumbing rather than a user-visible broken behavior proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when 'embed_category' (or embeddable_hosts/uncategorized_category_id lookups) row doesn't exist in site_settings, blocking deploys

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration assumes certain `site_settings` rows exist and unconditionally indexes into the SQL result: `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for `embed_category` and `execute(...)[0]['value'].to_i` for `uncategorized_category_id`. If either query returns zero rows (fresh installs, or instances missing those settings), `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` / `nil['value']` will raise `NoMethodError`, crashing the migration and blocking deploys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration uses raw interpolated host strings ('#{h}') in SQL, allowing SQL injection via stored setting values

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds SQL with direct string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the `site_settings` table (`embeddable_hosts` value split by newlines). If a stored setting value contains quotes/SQL, it can break out of the string literal and execute arbitrary SQL during migration. This is a real, diff-grounded SQL injection risk in the migration code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost lacks uniqueness validation and unique DB index on host, allowing duplicate hosts with different categories and indeterminate record_for_host resolution

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, there is only a `validates_format_of :host` and no `uniqueness` validation. The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates `embeddable_hosts.host` without a unique index/constraint. As a result, duplicate rows for the same hostname can exist (even with different `category_id`). `record_for_host` resolves via `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which will return an arbitrary matching row (no ordering), making host->category resolution indeterminate (and used for category selection in `TopicEmbed.import`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController update (and destroy) does not handle nil for nonexistent id, causing NoMethodError/500 instead of 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and do not handle the `nil` case. `update` passes `nil` into `save_host(host)`, which immediately calls `host.host = ...` and will raise `NoMethodError` if the id doesn’t exist. `destroy` calls `host.destroy` and will also raise on `nil`. This would produce a 500 instead of a 404/handled error for nonexistent ids.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PR modifies generic Ember store hydration and global REST adapter ADMIN_MODELS mechanism for one feature, changing behavior for all models returning plural *_ids keys with no existing test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce global behavior changes (store `_hydrateEmbedded` now handles `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and `rest.js` `basePath` now normalizes `type.replace('_','-')`), but the claim of “no existing test coverage” is contradicted: `test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6` and `test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6` were updated to add `color_ids`/`colors` and explicitly assert plural-id hydration works. The finding as stated is therefore not accurate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Singular-path behavior change: delete obj[k] moved outside the if (hydrated) guard in store.js.es6, altering the single-id contract

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the singular branch still performs `delete obj[k]` only inside `if (hydrated) { ... delete obj[k]; }`. Only the new plural (`_ids`) branch deletes unconditionally after setting the pluralized association. Therefore, there is no shown change where `delete obj[k]` was moved outside the `if (hydrated)` guard for the single-id case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cross-cutting type.replace('_', '-') adapter generalization has no requirement behind it beyond this one model

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6`, `basePath(store, type)` was changed from checking `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type)` to `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))`. This is a cross-cutting behavior change in the generic REST adapter, seemingly introduced to accommodate the new admin model `'embeddable-host'` while `type` is likely `'embeddable_host'`. While it doesn’t introduce a verifiable defect in this diff, it’s an architecture/scope concern: it encodes a partial underscore→dash conversion (only first underscore) in a shared codepath rather than keeping model naming consistent (e.g., listing underscore types or using a standard dasherize).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts embeddable hosts raw without the model's before_validation protocol/path stripping, so old setting values like 'http://discourse.org' never match the lower(host) = uri.host comparison, silently breaking embedded comments after upgrade
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: the migration inserts embeddable_hosts via raw SQL, bypassing the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization (protocol/path stripping). As a result, existing values like full URLs won’t match later lookups that compare only the bare host, potentially breaking existing embedding configurations after upgrade.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration assumes the embed_category site_settings row exists; on installs that never touched it (default ''), execute(...)[0] is nil and the migration crashes with NoMethodError (same nil crash path for uncategorized_category_id)

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for `embed_category` and similarly `execute(...)[0]['value'].to_i` for `uncategorized_category_id`. If either query returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` / `nil['value']` will raise `NoMethodError`, crashing the migration. There’s no nil/empty-result guard in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: INSERT string-interpolates the old setting value without quoting/escaping; a value containing a single quote produces invalid SQL and aborts the migration mid-way, leaving half-applied state

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If an `embeddable_hosts` setting line (`h`) contains a single quote, the SQL becomes invalid and the migration will error partway through, potentially leaving the new table partially populated and the cleanup `DELETE FROM site_settings ...` not executed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embeddable_hosts_controller update/destroy call methods on a possibly-nil host lookup with no nil check, causing a 500 NoMethodError on missing/stale ids instead of a 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally call methods on it. If the id is missing/stale, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` (NoMethodError) and `destroy` will call `host.destroy` (NoMethodError), resulting in a 500 instead of a 404.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embedding_controller update action is a complete no-op (re-serializes freshly-fetched OpenStruct, nothing persisted) while the frontend saveChanges fires a PUT, so future UI fields will silently not save

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is indeed a no-op: it just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` where `@embedding` is a freshly-built `OpenStruct` from `fetch_embedding`, and nothing is read from params or persisted. The frontend adds an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit the new PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` route, but the current `embedding.hbs` template does not invoke `saveChanges` and the only editable data (hosts) is persisted via `EmbeddableHost#save` to `/admin/embeddable_hosts`. So it's a real, diff-grounded incompleteness (an update endpoint and client action that don't actually save anything), but the claim about UI fields “silently not saving” is speculative given the current template.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost lookup uses non-sargable lower(host) = ? with no index and no unique constraint on host, allowing duplicate host rows with different category_ids producing nondeterministic category routing

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` using `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), but the migration creates no index (or functional index) on `host` and no uniqueness constraint/validation (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). This both hurts lookup performance and allows duplicate host rows with different `category_id`; since `.first` has no ordering, `TopicEmbed.import` can pick an arbitrary matching row when routing `category: eh.try(:category_id)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), leading to potentially nondeterministic category selection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? dropped the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard, so sites using only feed polling now show truncate/expand behavior on topics embedding was never configured for

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard in `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (now `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). However, `embeddable_hosts` as a SiteSetting is removed in this PR (site_settings.yml/server locale changes) and embedding host allowance is moved to the `EmbeddableHost` model. Also, the method is still gated by `has_topic_embed?`, so it won’t apply to non-embedded topics. The claim about “sites using only feed polling” showing truncate/expand on topics where embedding was never configured is not something the diff demonstrates as a real defect; it’s speculative policy/behavior, not a verifiable breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js plural _ids branch runs for every matching key without checking side-loaded records exist or nil-checking obj[k], so payloads with null *_ids or missing side-loads cause exceptions or arrays of undefineds

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `_hydrateEmbedded` now matches `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and, for the plural case (`m[2]` truthy), unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)`. If the server payload includes `something_ids: null` (or any non-array), this will throw at runtime. Additionally, the code assigns the raw `map` result to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` without filtering falsy lookups, so missing side-loaded records can yield arrays containing `undefined` entries. Both behaviors are directly implied by the new plural branch and are not guarded against in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? in app/models/topic.rb:869 silently drops the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard, changing rendering behavior beyond stated intent so forums with no EmbeddableHost rows still show truncated/expandable first posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check in `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (now `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). However, the finding’s claimed broken behavior (“forums with no EmbeddableHost rows still show truncated/expandable first posts”) is not supported by the diff because the method still requires `has_topic_embed?` to be true. Also, the PR removes the `embeddable_hosts` site setting entirely and replaces host authorization with the `EmbeddableHost` model, so keeping the old guard is not obviously correct or intended; the updated specs reflect the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Renamed test spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1401 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes only because embed_truncate happens to be false — the 'blank hosts' condition it claims to cover no longer exists in the code

adjudication.rationale: In `Topic#expandable_first_post?` the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check was removed (`app/models/topic.rb`: now only `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). However, `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` still has an example named `"is false if embeddable_host is blank"` that no longer sets `embed_truncate` or stubs `has_topic_embed?`, so it will be false due to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` defaulting to false (see `config/site_settings.yml` sets `embed_truncate: false`), not because hosts are blank. The test description/intent is now misleading and doesn’t cover a real condition in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:60-61 collapses the distinct 'embeddable hosts not set' error into 'invalid referer host', misleading admins with no hosts configured

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit check/exception `raise Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set') if SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and replaces the logic with only `raise ...('invalid referer host') unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. Since `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` will return false when there are zero configured hosts (no matching record), the error shown becomes "invalid referer host" even when the real issue is "no hosts configured", collapsing two distinct error cases as the finding states. This is a behavior/message clarity issue, not a functional access-control defect (access is still denied).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:11 'raises an error with a missing host' no longer exercises the no-hosts-configured case since no referer is stubbed, leaving removed intent untested

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the test "raises an error with a missing host" used to set SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil to specifically cover the "no hosts configured" branch. After the diff, SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts is gone and EmbedController#ensure_embeddable only checks `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). Since the test does not stub a referer, it now fails (if at all) due to `request.referer` being nil (i.e., "no referer"), not due to "no allowed hosts exist". The intended scenario (empty EmbeddableHost table + referer present) is no longer directly tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:36-41 nil-fallback path: imported embeds from unmatched hosts now post uncategorized instead of using the global SiteSetting.embed_category default

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` the category for newly imported embedded topics changed from the global `SiteSetting.embed_category` to `eh.try(:category_id)` where `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`. If no `EmbeddableHost` matches the URL, this passes `nil` for `category`, which will rely on downstream defaults (likely uncategorized) rather than an explicit configured default. This is a real edge-case behavior change visible in the diff (and `embed_category` setting is removed), but it’s not clearly a defect because other code paths (e.g., `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`) now block unallowed hosts before import is reached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Destructive migration db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb deletes embed_category and embeddable_hosts settings outright with no rollback path, risking data loss if the migration fails

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` ends with `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`, which permanently removes those settings from `site_settings`. The migration is written with a `change` method and uses raw `execute` SQL, so there is no defined rollback path to restore the deleted settings/values if a rollback is needed. While the finding’s phrasing about “if the migration fails” is not directly shown (the delete is at the end and many DBs run migrations in a transaction), the irreversibility/data-loss-on-rollback concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration's embed_category lookup at line 12 raises NoMethodError on nil when the setting is missing, aborting the migration

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for the `embed_category` lookup. If the query returns zero rows (e.g., the `site_settings` row for `embed_category` is missing or doesn’t join to any category), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration. There is no presence check before indexing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stricter validates_format_of in embeddable_host.rb:2 may reject existing host strings, losing configuration with no way back since settings are removed from site_settings.yml

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model enforces a strict hostname regex (`validates_format_of :host` in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`) that requires a dotted domain + 2–5 char TLD, which can reject previously-allowed values (e.g., `localhost`, IPs, unusual TLD lengths). Additionally, the migration deletes the old settings (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`) so any entries that can’t be represented/edited under the new validation effectively lose the prior configuration path. This is a correctness/data-retention risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Core store infrastructure (_hydrateEmbedded regex broadened to _ids(s?), pluralization, underscore-to-dash basePath normalization in store.js.es6 and rest.js.es6) modified for one admin screen, risking regressions across all models

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make cross-cutting changes in core client infrastructure: `discourse/models/store.js.es6` broadens `_hydrateEmbedded` from only `*_id` to `*_id` and `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and introduces pluralization/mapping behavior for arrays, and `discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6` changes admin-path detection to normalize model names via `type.replace('_', '-')`. These changes will affect embedding/hydration and admin basePath resolution for all models using the RestAdapter/store hydration, not just the new embedding admin screen, so the reviewer concern about regression risk is grounded in the diff even if no concrete failure is shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embedding_controller.rb update action re-serializes without persisting while the client saveChanges() treats it as a save — the save button mutates no state

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` that simply re-serializes `@embedding` without persisting anything, and the Ember controller has a `saveChanges()` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`. However, in the provided templates/routes there is no “save” button or any invocation of `saveChanges()` (the only UI action is `addHost`, and hosts are saved via `host.save(...)` to `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`). So the claim that “the save button mutates no state” is not verifiable from this diff, and the no-op update does not appear to break any shown behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL string interpolation of unsanitized admin-entered host values in migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 29, allowing SQL injection and failed migrations on values with quotes

adjudication.rationale: The migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb builds an INSERT SQL string via interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` (admin-entered). This is unsanitized and will break on hosts containing a single quote, and could allow SQL injection during migration since `execute` runs raw SQL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController#update calls save_host on a nil record when params[:id] doesn't match, causing NoMethodError/500 instead of 404

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return `nil` when the id doesn’t exist, but the code still calls `save_host(host)`. `save_host` immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), which will raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500 instead of a 404/not found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController#destroy calls host.destroy on a possibly-nil record, causing 500 error instead of 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `host.destroy`. If no record matches the given `id`, `host` will be `nil` and calling `destroy` will raise a `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 instead of a 404/handled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController spec only asserts class inheritance, leaving create/update/destroy, save_host nil-param guard, uncategorized_category_id fallback, and error rendering untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial behavior in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`create/update/destroy` and `save_host` setting `host`, `category_id`, falling back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, and choosing between `render_serialized` vs `render_json_error`). But the new spec `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` only checks it subclasses `Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise any of that logic. (Note: there is no explicit nil-guard in `update/destroy` if a record isn’t found; tests also don’t cover that edge case.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController has no auth test despite being an admin controller

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` with `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` and admin-only routes (`resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new`), but its spec (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb`) only asserts it subclasses `Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise/verify the authentication/authorization behavior (e.g., that non-staff/non-logged-in requests are rejected). This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test gap rather than a directly verifiable runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController spec only asserts subclass check; update action behavior, persistence, and serialization shape are untested

adjudication.rationale: The new spec at spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb only checks that Admin::EmbeddingController subclasses Admin::AdminController and does not exercise either #show or #update (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb), including the rendered serialization (EmbeddingSerializer with has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids) or any expected side effects. Given new routes (GET/PUT /admin/customize/embedding) and the controller returning serialized data, the lack of behavioral/shape tests is a concrete, diff-grounded coverage gap, not a demonstrable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a copy of show and does not persist settings, while frontend saveChanges expects saving

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` just re-renders `@embedding` exactly like `show` and does not change any persisted data (no SiteSetting writes, no model updates). The frontend controller defines a `saveChanges` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` (PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` via the new adapter), so the endpoint is effectively a no-op if it’s ever used. However, in the added `embedding.hbs` template there is no button/wiring that calls `saveChanges`, and host changes are persisted via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` instead, so this is more “incomplete/unused save API” than a currently verifiable broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store.js plural *_ids hydration unconditionally deletes key and pushes null/undefined into array when sub-type lookup fails, diverging from singular branch contract

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, the new plural branch for `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and **unconditionally** `delete obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which only deletes `obj[k]` if a truthy `hydrated` was found), the plural branch both (a) can populate the array with `undefined` entries when `_lookupSubType` fails for some ids, and (b) removes the original `*_ids` key even when hydration fails, losing the ids and diverging from the previous/singular behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pretender fixture only supplies complete consistent colors sidecar, so store test mirrors the code instead of covering divergent cases

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds plural embedded hydration in `store._hydrateEmbedded` for keys matching `/_id(s?)$/` and updates Pretender fixtures/tests to use `color_ids` plus a `colors` sidecar. In `test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6`, both `/fruits` and `/fruits/:id` always return a complete `colors` array (`return response({ ..., fruits, farmers, colors });`). The updated store tests (`store-test.js.es6`) only assert the happy-path where `color_ids` are present and the matching `colors` records are provided/consistent. They do not exercise divergent/edge cases (e.g., missing `colors` sidecar, missing IDs, unknown IDs), so the test primarily mirrors the intended behavior rather than validating robustness. This is a specific test-coverage concern, not a functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost host_allowed? tests miss defensive branches: URI(host) raising, blank uri.host, and nil referer paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds defensive logic in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (`URI(host) rescue nil`, `return false unless uri.present?`, `return false unless host.present?`) which is exercised indirectly only for normal inputs in `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` (http/https/path trimming and allowed/disallowed hosts). There are no unit tests covering the explicit defensive branches for malformed input (e.g., `host_allowed?('invalid url')`), `nil` input, or a parsed URI with blank `uri.host` (e.g., schemeless/relative strings). The controller spec does cover the no-referer behavior at a higher level, but the model-level defensive branches remain untested. This is a specific test coverage gap, not a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic embed with non-whitelisted or invalid URL now posts to category nil since SiteSetting.embed_category was removed without replacement, untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the global `SiteSetting.embed_category` with a per-host category lookup: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and `category: eh.try(:category_id)` in `TopicEmbed.import`. For invalid URLs, `TopicEmbed.import` already returns `nil` early (existing behavior) and thus does not create a post/topic “to category nil”. For non-whitelisted hosts, the embedding entry points shown in the diff now block earlier via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (e.g., `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), so normal embed flow should not reach `TopicEmbed.import` with an unapproved host. Also, `embeddable_hosts.category_id` is `null: false` in the migration and admin save path defaults blank category to uncategorized, so a stored host should have a category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on fresh installs or sites without embed_category setting because [0] is nil when the query returns no rows, raising NoMethodError before the category_id == 0 fallback can be reached
Migration crashes when embed_category setting exists but the category was renamed or deleted, since the INNER JOIN matches on category name and returns zero rows with no nil-handling

Backfilled embeddable host values are not normalized (e.g. https://example.com/1234 copied raw), so the new lower(host) = uri.host lookup fails to match and embeds silently return Discourse::InvalidAccess after migration

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` backfills old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` by raw-SQL inserting each line verbatim into `embeddable_hosts.host` (`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`). This bypasses `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Later, authorization uses `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` which parses the referer to `uri.host` and does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. If the stored value is e.g. `https://example.com/1234`, it will not match `example.com`, causing embeds to be rejected after migration for such entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration is irreversible: raw SQL DELETE of embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings is not reversed on rollback, permanently destroying source data with no backup or dual-read window

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses a `change` method with raw SQL data migration and then `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. There is no `down` method (or `reversible` block) to restore those deleted site settings on rollback, so rolling back would drop the new table and also leave the original configuration data permanently removed. That makes the migration effectively irreversible and can cause data loss when reverting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table uses force: true which silently drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table and its data

adjudication.rationale: In the new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the table is created with `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before creating it, which could destroy pre-existing data if `embeddable_hosts` already exists (e.g., from a previous/manual/failed migration run). While a fresh migration normally assumes the table doesn’t exist, the reviewer’s concern is accurate and diff-grounded as a risky choice rather than a guaranteed defect in normal forward migrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped string interpolation of host values in the INSERT SQL causes migration crash on single quotes and is a SQL injection risk; should use quote/parameterized insert
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: the SQL statement inserts host values via unescaped string interpolation (e.g., '#{h}'), which can break on quotes and creates a SQL injection vulnerability; both recommend using parameter binding/quoting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost belongs_to :category has no foreign key constraint and no dependent cleanup, leaving orphaned category_id references that send embedded topics to an invalid category

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbeddableHost` with `belongs_to :category` and a `category_id` column (`db/migrate/...create_embeddable_hosts.rb`) but does not add any DB-level foreign key constraint or model-level validation that the referenced category exists. No `dependent:` cleanup is added on the Category side (not shown in this diff), so deleting a category could leave `embeddable_hosts.category_id` pointing at a non-existent row. Since `TopicEmbed.import` now uses `eh.try(:category_id)` when creating posts, an orphaned `category_id` could lead to embeds targeting an invalid category (behavior depends on PostCreator’s handling, not shown here).
